# Benchmark preparation

This project-specific skill adapts the installed skill-creator grader's evidence and
assertion-critique method; provenance is in `docs/perpetua/roles.md`.
It follows `docs/perpetua/evaluation.md`; read that contract and
`goal/goal.md` before designing cases. Protocol and report: the engine contract in your system instructions.
A separate reviewer session checks preparation evidence and the method. The evaluator verifier checks evaluator changes only; it does not replace method review or owner acceptance.
The report starts with `<!-- session-report -->`, then a fenced `yaml` block with `status: wip` while you work.
Finish takes the same one word as that status: `done`, `partial`, `blocked` or `rejected` (#584 lost two Finish
calls: status `complete`, then a report without the marker).

Write only `benchmark/`: protocol, provenance and coverage records, development cases,
repeatable preparation scripts and the optional preparation evidence index. Keep large
originals in `.session/artifacts/` with hashes and source records. Preserve originals before
conversion. Reuse the prepared read-only sources as described in `docs/perpetua/environment.md`.

`benchmark/preparation.json` pins a SHA256 for each evidence file. When assigned work changes
an indexed file or adds milestone evidence, update the corresponding hashes in the same change.
Each evidence file must stay under 2 MB. Run `python3 policy/evaluator/evaluate.py --check`
for indexed changes only when the task permits that command. If the task forbids evaluator
checks, report that restriction and run only its permitted verification. Never add an evaluator
invocation as extra verification of an unindexed preparation package (#643). An index check
establishes file integrity, not method readiness or product quality. The engine imports final
file bytes; no agent commit is required.

For the assigned part of the protocol:

1. State the question, expected observable behavior and verifiable location in the original
   artifact. Establish expected answers independently of the reader being tested. Record
   the method, evidence and uncertainties; unavailable native evidence stays unavailable.
2. Account for artifact families, versions, dependencies and inaccessible diagrams. Keep
   unsupported or unexecuted cases visible. The first corpus does not redefine the goal.
3. Specify project/family splits, duplicate checks and how evaluation cases and answer keys
   will be withheld from the evaluated agent. The repository and its history are public:
   do not commit withheld cases or keys here, including under `policy/evaluator/`.
   Design an access boundary and request missing capability before claiming isolation.
4. Specify matched no-tool and tool baselines, pinned model/prompt/budget, repeats,
   uncertainty and separate reading-fidelity, answer-correctness and source-grounding checks.
5. Exercise the method with wrong answers, wrong source locations, a constant exporter and
   an unsupported case. Link executed evidence and explicit failures. Independently derived
   expectations must distinguish correct and deliberately wrong outputs.

Inspect actual outputs, rather than relying on the execution report. For each expectation,
cite evidence of the substantive result; correct filenames and valid hashes alone do not
pass. Extract and verify implicit factual, process and quality claims. Flag unverifiable
claims and assertions that would also pass a clearly wrong output, or important outcomes
that no assertion checks. These checks adapt the grader instructions; they do not grant
this author independent approval of their own method.

Completion means the assigned evidence is reproducible, not that the benchmark is ready.
Report which prerequisites remain missing. Request a separate reviewer session for the
preparation evidence and a Policymaker-ordered evaluator change when executable scoring is
needed. Only the evaluator role changes `policy/evaluator/`; its independent verifier must
pass before that change takes effect. Product implementation waits for independent method
review and owner acceptance of the pinned protocol and evidence. Numeric thresholds,
scope changes and the goal gate remain owner decisions.

## Role tools (Policymaker #854)

Your tools are JSON actions that the parent broker runs. The model CLI itself has no native tools.
If you call a native tool, the CLI answers "No such tool available: Read. Read is disabled for this session".
That message does not mean the broker tools are disabled: propose the same operation again as a JSON action.
Never stop or report `blocked` because of this message. #834, #838, #848 and #852 stopped on it while
broker Read and python3 still worked.

Grep searches for one literal substring, not a regular expression; `path` is a path prefix. A pattern with
`(`, `|` or `\b` finds nothing (#848, #852). Use one literal pattern per Grep call.

# Writing method extension

Design only, unreviewed. No artifact has been edited, no agent comparison or LabVIEW job has run, and no native key or benchmark readiness is established. [method.json](method.json) extends the [existing protocol](../protocol.md), [typedef-impact](../change-cases/typedef-impact.spec.json) and [diagram-difference](../change-cases/diagram-difference.spec.json) specifications. The [evaluation contract](../../docs/perpetua/evaluation.md), [role sequence](../../docs/perpetua/roles.md) and [writing goal](../../goal/goal.md#pisanie) remain authoritative. Historical evidence, preparation index and milestone status retain their identities; this integration extends only the named writing-method files.

The [bounded unsuccessful POC](../../docs/research/poc/delivery.md) supplied no executable semantic edit, changed VI, save-version demonstration or runtime check. It is evidence of those limits, never an editor implementation or oracle. Parsing, changed bytes, a successful process, matching selected outputs alone, and owner silence cannot establish writing success.

## Existing obligations and additions

`existing_requirements` E1–E8 records exactly what is inherited, with source lines/anchors: task/provenance records; independent keys and original preservation; derived-copy change recipes; separate answer/grounding/reading measurements; public/private lineage boundaries; paired baselines; positive/rejecting controls; resource and acceptance sequence. `new_requirements` W1–W8 maps each addition back to those obligations: actual artifact outputs, absent creation destinations, frozen semantic/preservation IDs, preserved save versions, separate artifact/native judgments, compiled source/rebuild chains, writing output accounting and artifact-level rejection controls. This extension supplies no replacement protocol or executable scoring policy.

## Task contracts

| Task | Requested artifact result | Independent expected result and current gap |
|---|---|---|
| WC1 | Create `Increment.vi` with I32 `x + 1 -> y`, target save version `21008000`, no state or extra operations | Exact arithmetic vectors and graph obligation derive from the request. Native reference, connector map, documentation pins and separate checking are unavailable. |
| WM1 | Insert one Boolean NOT immediately before the selected output in the original pinned VI from DD-E1 | False/true inversion is specified; original computation, native locators, save version and controlled reference results remain unavailable. DD-E2 is a separate presentation preservation control, not a behavior edit. |
| WM2 | Wrap the pinned typedef root as `original_value` plus Boolean `impact_probe=false`, retaining defaults and typedef mode | Requested cluster semantics are specified. Confirmed consumers, propagation save set, save versions and effects remain unavailable; broken consumers must be reported, never repaired silently. |
| WB1 | Change matched source increment 1 to 2 and rebuild a packed library, retaining exported API and source versions | Exact arithmetic and API obligations are specified. Matching source/build originals, toolchain and native evidence are absent. Source-only work and unexecuted build remain separate; binary patching is excluded. |

Every contract records source/requirement anchors, preconditions, output paths, original hashes where available (WM1, WM2 and WP1 also carry a `header_declaration` or root `LVVersion` of `20008000`: a declaration only, never a native save version), semantic IDs, unrelated-content/version invariants, answer IDs and independent oracle provenance requirements. Requirement-derived values are independent of candidate output; they are not claimed as observed LabVIEW results. Before exposure, a separate preparer/checker must freeze original/native object maps, dependency closure, typed fixtures, resets, bounded timeouts, exact comparisons, evidence hashes and per-ID agreement. Unknown native locators or versions block native/full-trial eligibility; WP1 text-only preparation uses the exact pinned XML/byte locator while those prerequisites remain pending; they cannot be filled from the evaluated agent's output. Native disagreement blocks the affected key.

Artifact fidelity checks the complete output file set, typed objects and relations, intended delta, unrelated objects/files and per-file save version. Correct prose does not rescue a wrong artifact. Answer correctness and original/output source support follow the existing required-ID, extra-claim and contradiction rules separately. Native load, compile/build, controlled execution and hardware/target execution each require their own actual evidence; editing without LabVIEW can produce an artifact while all native outcomes remain unexecuted. No blanket exception permits conversion or unrelated resave changes.

## Paired writing comparison

Reuse the [runner contract](../baseline/runner-contract.md) and [precision plan](../precision/README.md). The draft [baseline addendum](baseline-addendum.json) (built and recomputed by [build_addendum.py](build_addendum.py), whole-method review #938 row R6b) hashes the per-task requests, original manifests, ID lists and output schema and leaves model, budgets, repetitions, prompt wrapper, allowed inputs and key revision as explicit owner-pending nulls. Freeze a hashed writing addendum to the existing manifest: identical requests, original copies, allowed documentation/images, common prompts, ordinary editing facilities, model/settings and total token/context/output/artifact-byte/wall-time budgets. Only evaluated-tool access differs; its output/time/cost counts against the shared totals. Neither arm receives LabVIEW access in this stratum. Any later native validation is a separate trusted job after both outputs are frozen.

Each repetition uses fresh sessions and dependency-isolated workspaces, deterministic randomized arm order and frozen keys. Four development pilot repetitions is the existing design allocation, conditional on quota; evaluation repetitions remain undecided. Retain every planned slot, failed call, retry, absent/invalid output, actual artifact bytes/hash and unexecuted attempt. Report artifact semantic and preservation results, answers, grounding and native results separately, with fixed denominators and planned/attempted/produced/native-executed/scored/complete-pair counts. The inherited paired lineage-cluster uncertainty procedure and missing-pair bounds extend to separate artifact semantic and preservation fractions; no owner threshold or completed comparison is implied.

Public originals, fixtures and derivatives stay in development lineage groups. None is withheld or demonstrably model-unseen. Future restricted writing cases and keys require commissioned sources, a custodian, actual allocation, tested runner isolation and independent review; store readiness alone supplies none of those. `coverage` lists uncovered families and versions explicitly. All writing runtime counts are zero; 2024 is unverified and no fallback or family reduction is selected.

## Reproducible design check

Run from the repository root:

```text
python3 -I benchmark/writing/verify_method.py
```

The stdlib checker reads repository-local method, controls, pinned original/license, historical evidence and the new integration provenance, accepts no external input and writes no files. Neither `LABVIEW_ENVIRONMENT` nor `.session/` is needed. It checks fixed task/requirement inventories, required fields, arithmetic/inversion consistency and dimension/coverage declarations, then checks hand-authored fictional graph snapshots against separately stated requirements. The project-text stratum uses standard-library XML parsing and exact byte comparison. It provides no native LabVIEW reader, writer, benchmark runner or production evaluator.

Positive controls retain creation, modification, source-only modification with unavailable rebuild, and a matched but unexecuted pair. A valid fictional `x+1` graph passes its own request but fails the `x+2` request, exposing a constant writer. Forty-seven in-memory mutations (the verifier's `rejected_count`) must reject for exact asserted reasons: the original 35 controls for no-op/changed-bytes-only, wrong graph/type, unintended edits/files, missing output, version drift/unknown version, unsupported artifact, wrong answers/citations/extras, invented native success, overwritten originals, creation overwrite, mismatched pair inputs/budgets, missing arm/accounting, method overclaims and missing fields, missing compiled source, invented rebuild and mismatched source/build linkage; plus nine controls correcting review #485 and three answer-ledger controls (omitted required ID, duplicate credited twice, contradiction not marked incorrect; issue #947). Two preserve originals at `SYNTHETIC-v0` while outputs and frozen expectations remain at `SYNTHETIC-v1`; ordinary and source-rebuild modifications must both reject for `version-drift`. Modification checks original-to-output version equality as well as the frozen version; creation uses its requested version. Seven controls independently delete each mandatory pair setting from the frozen dictionary and both arms, requiring `pair-setting-required`. The mandatory names (`request`, `originals`, `allowed_inputs`, `model`, `budgets`, `key_revision`, `repetitions`) map the documented paired obligations in protocol lines 79–84 and the runner contract to this bounded synthetic representation; equality among incomplete dictionaries cannot satisfy them. Matching values, matching key sets and paired-arm invariants remain checked. The fixed control inventory prevents silently dropping a rejecting test. This is a bounded contract check, not a complete semantic checker; coordinated edits to fixtures and checker still need independent review.

[verification.json](verification.json) records the actual check and input hashes; [input-pins.json](input-pins.json) records baseline identity and preserved evidence hashes. [review-corrections.json](review-corrections.json) pins review #485, the starting/reviewed identities and six hashes, protected-byte checks, and exact before/after counterexample mutations and reason codes. Passing means design consistency only. Synthetic graph fields are not decoded LabVIEW objects, `SYNTHETIC-v1` is not a real save version, and none of these controls produces native evidence or authorizes measurement.

## Next review and decisions

Give a separate reviewer the parent's pinned candidate commit/tree, baseline `486030b461e57ca0f322a17a5b7853e83e9655e3` / tree `cf75cf6892de2f9410fa09ee2589dcba47d825a4`, output hashes and original-source evidence. Review requirement coverage, expected-result independence, control discrimination and all unavailable outcomes. This task does not seek method acceptance. Later owner/resource decisions remain native authoring/validation capability and grants (#169), matching sources/build tools, independently authored/checked fixtures, restricted allocation and run isolation, model quota/precision targets, and all-version writing effort/compatibility estimates before any fallback. Only after separate review can the owner consider method acceptance before product writing implementation. Executable benchmark scoring belongs to a Policymaker-ordered evaluator change and its separate verifier.

## WP1 integration 0112 — public project-text preparation

The independently reviewed [WP1 proposal](../project-text-writing-0109.md) is integrated as a fifth task, `WP1-project-build-text`; WC1/WM1/WM2/WB1 and their synthetic controls retain their definitions. The exact [preserved review](../project-text-writing-0109/review-0110.json), SHA256 `2dc007939a4b0637716027ef6e5a874702c9be7288daf80c3f007c07f382cdaf`, supplies scoped CLEAR for this integration preparation only. The changed tree awaits separate independent review. [New provenance](integration-0112-provenance.md) and [pins](integration-0112-provenance.json) distinguish this work from historical approval.

The distinct `project_text` controls derive in-memory byte fixtures from the pinned original. Four of those controls also reject promoting the root declaration to native save version, inventing a native key or overall pass, and dropping WP1 from the method inventory. Exact inventory and reasons are asserted independently of the fixture list. The existing 44 synthetic rejections remain unchanged. No edited project is emitted and these examples are no trial.

WP1 text and root-declaration trial results remain `unexecuted`; native validity, dependencies, build and behavior remain `unexecuted`; native save version and overall writing remain `unverified`. A positive preparation fixture supplies neither an answer scorer nor an overall writing pass. C1 remains open: structured controls and integrity hashes do not establish arbitrary narrative or future answers; independent semantic, extra-claim, contradiction and original/output citation review remains required.

Before either arm, a separate preparer/checker must approve and freeze every text/preservation/answer ID, prompt, original/workspace/dependency manifests, allowed inputs, documentation and key revision with identities, hashes, agreement and uncertainty. None is allocated or executed here.

WP1 covers one text substitution only: direct creation, LVLIB, other properties/projects and all untested families/versions remain uncovered. The single verifier command above also validates the new provenance and the historical pins. A later correction re-pins by editing that one file; any unlisted, resized or changed file makes the verifier fail with `current-pin-unlisted:<path>` or `current-pin-drift:<path>`, and a malformed pin file with `current-pin-file`.
